messages.content: Predict one human decision in a one-shot public-goods experiment. Each person receives 20 tokens, privately chooses a contribution to a group account and keeps the tokens not contributed. The total group contribution is multiplied by the announced group-return multiplier and divided equally among EVERY group member, including those who contributed nothing. A person’s first-stage earnings are 20 minus their own contribution plus this equal public return. The same group includes the participant, so the stated group size counts self. Group members may decide before or after one another; records are matched into groups only after data collection, with no actual peer decisions or realized group payoff available at these response stages. The participation fee is USD 1.00. Tokens determine the chance of a USD 2 bonus, rather than being paid at a fixed cash exchange rate. The contribution is all or nothing: either 0 or 20 tokens. The released record does not specify the precise token-to-prize-probability conversion. Before contributing, participants are told their contribution will be revealed to some or all members, then each member can choose a preferred partner for a new task; a person cannot continue that new task if nobody selects them. In its later conditional stage, choose among three shown members or choose nobody. After selecting a partner, receive six additional tokens and choose to give that partner either 0 or all 6. Tokens not given are kept; a gift of 6 becomes 18 tokens for the partner. Predict the first-stage contribution. Output only 0 or 20 tokens, without explanation.

Group size: 40 including you. The total contribution multiplier is 1.6; each member therefore receives 1.6/40 of every token contributed, including their own. 
Stable personal descriptors collected at the end of the study: age 47 years; gender Female.
How many tokens does this person contribute now?
